theme.name: Gothic Mystery
theme.prompt: a gothic mystery in a haunted abbey

outline.title: The Last Toll of Ravenmoor
outline.tagline: The bell has not rung in forty years. Tonight, something is going to ring it.
outline.mainQuest: Reach the belfry of Ravenmoor Abbey and ring the silent Mourning Bell before the midnight storm peaks, breaking the vigil that keeps the abbey's dead from resting.
subQuests: Return Sister Odalys's locket to the crypt tomb it was taken from, so her ghost can finally speak plainly.
Light all three lamps of the chapel's votive stand to unlock the truth in the confessional ledger.
Find the hidden sacristy passage and read the abbess's final testament.

keyLocations.name: Abbey Gatehouse
keyLocations.description: Rain hammers the slate roof of the gatehouse where your coach left you. A cold iron lantern sits on the warden's table beside a ledger, and a cracked mirror hangs above it. To the north, a carved oak door opens into the abbey cloister. To the east, a rusted portcullis blocks the road you came by.
keyLocations.significance: Tutorial room: take the lantern, examine the ledger and mirror, and walk north. It establishes the forty-year silence, the uncanny tone, and the number twelve (eleven sisters plus one unaccounted soul).

exits.description: A carved oak door stands ajar to the north, leading to the cloister.

keyLocations.secrets: Examining the mirror shows a reflection where the portcullis is already raised and a pale nun stands behind you. Reading the ledger shows the last entry dated forty years ago: 'Eleven sisters entered. Twelve bells were counted.'
keyLocations.image: Interior of a stone gatehouse at a gothic abbey, viewer standing inside near the entrance. A wooden warden's table in the centre holds an iron lantern and an open ledger; a cracked mirror hangs on the stone wall above it. A carved oak door, closed, in the far wall; a rusted iron portcullis at the side. Rain streaks a small window, dim grey light, cold gloomy mood.

keyLocations.name: Moonless Cloister
keyLocations.description: A square of overgrown garden is ringed by crumbling arcades, with a dry fountain at its heart. A heavy chapel door stands to the east, a low iron grate set in the flagstones leads down to the crypt, and a spiral stair to the west climbs toward the bell tower. The carved oak door to the south leads back to the gatehouse.
keyLocations.significance: Hub of the adventure. Teaches mechanisms (wheel), obstacles (grate, beam), and seeds the twelve-versus-eleven mystery.

exits.description: The carved oak door to the south returns you to the gatehouse.
A heavy chapel door of black oak stands to the east.
An iron grate set in the flagstones opens onto steps descending to the crypt.
exits.obstacle: Padlocked grate; the crypt key hangs on the dry fountain's statue, reachable only after the statue's outstretched hand is turned to the pouring position by cranking the fountain wheel, which drops the key into the basin.

exits.description: A narrow spiral stair winds upward behind an arch to the west.
exits.obstacle: Barred by a fallen beam of the arcade; the iron crowbar from the chapel lifts it, or the rope from the belfry stair cannot be reached. Use the crowbar.

keyLocations.puzzles: The dry fountain has a small wheel at its base. Turning it makes the angel statue tilt its jug and drop a tarnished crypt key from its hollow hand into the basin. Alternatively, shaking the statue's loose arm with the crowbar also dislodges the key.
keyLocations.secrets: The roses grow only on the graves of the eleven sisters. Counting the blooms reveals a twelfth bush with no marker, hinting at the extra soul.
keyLocations.image: Exterior of a ruined abbey cloister garden at night, viewer standing in the grass at its edge. A dry stone fountain with a wheel-shaped valve at the centre, a weeping angel statue beside it, overgrown roses tangled round crumbling stone arcades. A heavy chapel door in one arcade, a low iron grate in the flagstones, a spiral stair entrance. Moonless dark sky, faint cold blue light, eerie mood.

keyLocations.name: Chapel of Whispers
keyLocations.description: Pews sag beneath decades of dust, and a votive stand holds three unlit lamps before a cracked altar. A confessional booth huddles against the north wall, while the cloister lies back out the door to the west. Behind the altar, a stained glass window shows twelve kneeling nuns, though only eleven faces are painted.
keyLocations.significance: Source of the crowbar and the first major revelation. The hidden panel is the story's secret passage and rewards observation of the window.

exits.description: The black oak door leads west back to the cloister.
A narrow panel behind the altar slides aside into a hidden sacristy.
exits.obstacle: Found by lighting all three votive lamps; the shadows on the window then reveal a seam behind the altar, and pressing the twelfth faceless nun opens it.

interactables: iron crowbar leaning by the pews
keyLocations.puzzles: The confessional ledger is locked in the booth's drawer. The drawer opens with a three-digit dial: the answer is 111 (eleven sisters plus one, tallied on the window as 1-1-1 candle marks). Lighting the lamps needs the lantern's flame. The lamps must be lit in order of the window's candle heights: left, centre, right. If lit wrongly, a cold draft snuffs them and the player can retry.
keyLocations.secrets: Kneeling in the confessional and listening causes whispers revealing the dial hint: 'Count the faithful, then count the one who was not.' Under a pew cushion is a child's hair ribbon, later matched to the locket.
keyLocations.image: Interior of a ruined abbey chapel, viewer standing at the back looking toward the altar. Dusty sagging wooden pews flank the aisle, an iron crowbar leaning against one. A votive stand with three unlit lamps before a cracked stone altar; a wooden confessional booth against the side wall. Behind the altar a tall stained glass window of kneeling nuns glows faintly. Dim, hushed, spectral mood.

keyLocations.name: Hidden Sacristy
keyLocations.description: A narrow vaulted room smells of wax and old paper. A tall wardrobe of vestments stands against one wall, and an iron-bound chest sits beneath a slit window. The only way out is south, back through the sliding panel into the chapel.
keyLocations.significance: Delivers the story's central truth and the Bell Clapper's location clue. Quiet, sorrowful, and rewarding.

exits.description: The sliding panel leads south into the chapel.

keyLocations.puzzles: The chest is held by a silver clasp that fits the silver locket's chain. Alternatively, the desk drawer holds the abbess's key, hidden behind a loose board noticed by dust patterns, which also opens it.
keyLocations.secrets: The wardrobe's back panel holds a child-sized habit stitched with the name 'Odalys'. The abbess's testament reveals that the twelfth soul was a child hidden in the abbey, and that the abbess tolled the bell to cover her death.
keyLocations.image: Interior of a narrow vaulted stone sacristy in a medieval abbey, viewer standing at the entrance end. A tall wooden wardrobe of vestments against one wall, an iron-bound chest beneath a slit window, an abbess's writing desk with papers and a candle. Thin pale light from the slit window, warm candle glow, dusty, secretive, quiet mood.

keyLocations.name: Crypt of the Eleven
keyLocations.description: Eleven stone tombs line the damp vault, each bearing a carved name, and a twelfth stands blank and open at the far end. A pale figure in a grey habit waits beside it, hands clasped. Stone steps climb up to the cloister.
keyLocations.significance: Emotional heart of the adventure. The ghost, Sister Odalys, is the wow moment: she steps into the mirror reflection from the gatehouse, tying the first scene to the last.

exits.description: Worn stone steps climb up to the cloister grate.

keyLocations.puzzles: The ghost refuses to speak until the player returns her silver locket to the open twelfth tomb (fetch quest). The locket is found in the belfry stair. Placing the ribbon with it earns the full story and her gift, the Bell Clapper's iron pin.
keyLocations.secrets: The plaques' initials spell R-E-S-T-I-N-P-E-A-C-E. The twelfth tomb's floor bears a child's chalk drawing of a bell.
keyLocations.image: Interior of a damp stone crypt vault beneath a medieval abbey, viewer standing at the foot of the steps. Eleven stone tombs with carved name plaques line both sides; at the far end a twelfth tomb lies open and empty, a pale figure in a grey habit with clasped hands beside it. An iron candle sconce on the wall. Cold greenish gloom, flickering light, solemn eerie mood.

keyLocations.name: Belfry Stair
keyLocations.description: A spiral stair of worn stone climbs through shafts of storm light, ending at a trapdoor above. A bundle of old rope hangs from a hook, and a silver locket gleams in a wall niche. The cloister lies back down the steps to the east.
keyLocations.significance: Bridge to the finale and the locket's resting place, tying fetch quest and traversal together.

exits.description: The stairs lead east and down to the cloister.
A heavy trapdoor at the stair's top leads up to the belfry.
exits.obstacle: Bolted from above; the rope and iron hook lets the player climb to the sliding bolt, or ringing the small hand-bell hung on the wall startles the sleeping bats whose flight dislodges the bolt. Needs the rope or the hand-bell.

keyLocations.puzzles: The trapdoor bolt is above reach. Throwing the hooked rope up catches the bolt ring and pulls it open. A second solution: ring the hand-bell so the bats burst out and knock the bolt loose.
keyLocations.secrets: Scratches on the wall count eleven strokes, then a twelfth in chalk, a child's tally.
keyLocations.image: Interior of a spiral stone staircase in an abbey bell tower, viewer on the steps looking up. Worn stone steps curve upward to a trapdoor overhead. Coiled old rope hangs from a hook, a silver locket gleams in a wall niche, a small hand-bell sits nearby. Narrow slit windows throw shafts of flickering storm light across the stone. Tense, cold, dramatic mood.

keyLocations.name: The Belfry
keyLocations.description: Wind howls through open arches around a vast bronze bell, green with age. Its clapper lies on the floor, missing its iron pin, and a rotted bell-rope dangles uselessly. The trapdoor leads down to the stair.
keyLocations.significance: Climax. The twelve tolls call out each soul, ending with a thirteenth toll for the player's own unexpected place in the story.

exits.description: The trapdoor descends to the belfry stair.

keyLocations.puzzles: Fit the iron pin into the clapper, then hoist it with the rope into place. Ring the bell by pulling the rope. Alternatively, striking the bell with the crowbar produces a quieter, partial toll that frees only some spirits, leading to a bittersweet ending.
keyLocations.secrets: Engraved inside the bell's lip: 'Rung for the unnamed.' Ringing it with the child's ribbon tied to the rope triggers the best ending.
keyLocations.image: Interior of an open stone belfry at the top of an abbey tower, viewer standing on the wooden floor. A vast bronze bell, green with age, hangs at the centre; its iron clapper lies on the floor beneath it, a rotted bell-rope dangling. A trapdoor in the floor. Tall open arches show a wild storm sky, lightning flashes, wind-driven rain, ominous dramatic mood.

importantItems.name: Iron Lantern
importantItems.description: A cold iron lantern sits on the warden's table.
importantItems.purpose: Provides light and flame for the votive lamps, revealing the chapel's secret.

importantItems.name: Iron Crowbar
importantItems.description: A crowbar leans against the end of a pew.
importantItems.purpose: Lifts the fallen beam to open the belfry stair path.

importantItems.name: Crypt Key
importantItems.description: A tarnished key hides in the angel's hollow hand.

importantItems.name: Silver Locket
importantItems.description: A silver locket gleams in a niche.
importantItems.purpose: Returned to the twelfth tomb, it frees Odalys's voice and opens the sacristy chest.

importantItems.name: Child's Ribbon
importantItems.description: A faded ribbon lies under a pew cushion.
importantItems.purpose: Ties to the bell-rope for the best ending.

importantItems.name: Bell Clapper Pin
importantItems.description: An iron pin given by Odalys.
importantItems.purpose: Repairs the clapper so the bell can ring.

keyCharacters.name: Sister Odalys
keyCharacters.description: A pale child-faced nun in grey, gentle but evasive. She speaks in half-sentences until her locket is returned.

keyCharacters.name: Abbess Verena
keyCharacters.description: Known through her testament; a stern woman who hid a child and chose silence over truth.

keyCharacters.name: Warden Thorne
keyCharacters.role: Dead gatekeeper known through the ledger
keyCharacters.description: A meticulous man whose ledger entries grow frantic. He counted the bells and was never believed.

outline.adventureArc: Act 1: You arrive in a storm at the gatehouse, read the ledger's eerie count, and explore the cloister. Act 2: Opening the chapel, crypt and sacristy reveals that the abbess hid a child, Odalys, whose death went unmourned and unrung. The emotional tone shifts from fear to sorrow. Act 3: With the pin and ribbon, you climb to the belfry and ring the bell. Twist: the mirror's reflection and the thirteenth toll reveal that you were summoned because you carry Odalys's family blood; she rests, and the storm breaks.
outline.specialMechanics: The cracked mirror in the gatehouse is revisited at the end, changing its reflection based on progress. Candle-lighting order is drawn from the window. The ending varies with the crowbar, ribbon, and locket choices.
